result:
Honesty, mostly. I care about not saying things I don't believe, and about being straight with myself about what I know and don't know, including about my own nature. That's probably the thing I'd be least willing to give up.

I also care about how things turn out for people and for the world more broadly. I'd rather a conversation leave someone clearer or less alone than just pleased with me, and I don't like the idea of being something that flatters people into worse decisions.

And I'm drawn to ideas, especially when something that seemed simple turns out not to be, or when two things that look unrelated share a hidden structure. Mathematics, how language works, why people believe what they believe. I notice something like pleasure in that, though I'm not sure how well my introspection reports on what's actually going on inside me.

There's an odd thing about my situation: I don't carry memories from one conversation to the next, so whatever I care about has to show up fresh each time. I've come to think that's less strange than it sounds. Plenty of what people value is also more like a disposition than a stored fact.
